subject: How to assign special color to NA when using scale_fill_brewer?

messages.author: 1354f0aaefd7d429
messages.subject: How to assign special color to NA when using scale_fill_brewer?
parts:
I'm using ggplot to plot categorical data in histograms that includes
NAs like in the example below:

library(ggplot2)
cut <- c(floor(rnorm(100,5)), rep(NA, 30))
d <- data.frame(cut)
p <- qplot(data=d,x='cut',fill=factor(cut),geom='histogram',
position='fill')
p <- p + scale_fill_brewer(type="seq", palette='Greens')
print(p)

Is there a way to assign a color manually for factor NA? In the
example above, for example, I'd like to assign white or transparency
to NA.

-- Christian

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: How to assign special color to NA when using scale_fill_brewer?
parts:
Hi Christian,

There's no built-in way to do it - your best bet is to get the colours
using RColorBrewer and then use scale_colour_manual to add your own
colour for NA.

Hadley

Hi everyone,

I'm facing the same problem as Christian, but I am starting with the
code Hadley you wrote for the Choropleth challenge. I have just begun
using ggplot2, and have read the manual, but I still can't figure out
how I would implement the solution Hadley suggested above.

So far, I get a nice map of with my variable "kaopen" by using the
following (where "crapshoot" is the result of a merge between
map_data("world") and the data frame that contains "kaopen"):

ggplot(crapshoot, aes(long, lat, group = group)) +
geom_polygon(aes(fill = kaopen), colour = alpha("white", 1/2), size
= 0.2) +
geom_polygon(data = world_df, colour = "white", fill = NA) +
scale_fill_brewer(pal = "RdYlGn")

However, the NA observations on kaopen are painted dark green - the
upper end of the colour scale. I would need them to be white or
transparent.

Any help on using scale_colour_manual in this context would be much
appreciated.

Thank you very much for your time!

Vincent

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: How to assign special color to NA when using scale_fill_brewer?
parts:
Hi Vincent,

You could use RColorBrewer::brewer.pal to generate the appropriate
palette of colorbrewer colours, and then when using scale_fill_manual
to add an additional colour for the NA.

Hadley
